description: I love how space tech solves real problems (like using satellites to track climate change). I excel in physics and CS (I built a Python planetary orbit simulator!) and collaborate on science fairs. Outside class, I follow NASA missions, volunteer at a science museum, and co-host a teen space news podcast. Most importantly, I listen first—great ideas come from everyone.
summary:
Pulse of Terra is an interactive, multi-sensory web application that transforms NASA’s Earth Information Center (EIC) satellite visualizations into real-time, harmonious musical soundscapes. While EIC data reveals critical planetary shifts, relying solely on visual graphics creates barriers for blind and low-vision individuals and limits emotional engagement with complex climate data.

By applying physics-inspired acoustic mapping and Python-driven data analysis, Pulse of Terra translates pixel-level environmental metrics—such as atmospheric CO₂ concentrations, ocean surface temperatures, and sea-ice extent—into dynamic pitch, rhythm, and timbre synchronized frame-by-frame with EIC animations. Users can "play" Earth’s climate timeline like a jukebox, isolating specific environmental layers as individual musical instruments. Bridging rigorous astrophysical data processing with accessible science communication, Pulse of Terra makes Earth science inclusive, intuitive, and deeply resonant—allowing everyone to not just see, but truly hear the changing heartbeat of our planet.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Pulse of Terra acts as a real-time audiovisual synthesizer powered by NASA Earth observation datasets. Users select an EIC visualization track (e.g., Global Temperature Anomalies, Arctic Sea Ice Minimum, or Aerosol Optical Depth) on an intuitive jukebox interface.

  • Data Extraction & Physics Mapping: A backend pipeline samples color gradients, spatial distribution, and temporal rate-of-change from each EIC video frame. Using harmonic acoustic principles, these values are mapped to musical parameters in real time—for instance, rising temperatures shift harmonic frequencies upward, while rapid seasonal shifts alter tempo and percussion density.
  • Multi-Track "Stem" Mixing: Inspired by audio production workflows, users can mute, solo, or blend different environmental variables (such as pairing greenhouse gas levels with global precipitation) to hear how Earth’s interconnected systems interact.
  • Guided Audio Narration Mode: Designed with museum visitors and visually impaired users in mind, an optional "Podcast Mode" provides concise, spoken context alongside spatial audio cues to explain what the changing sounds represent scientifically.

Tools, Languages, and Technologies Used

  • Data Processing & Backend: Python (utilizing NumPy, OpenCV, and Pandas to extract pixel intensity, RGB-to-value mapping, and time-series gradients from EIC visual frames and NASA Earthdata).
  • Real-Time Audio Synthesis: Web Audio API and Tone.js (for low-latency browser-based polyphonic synthesis, frequency modulation, and spatial panning), paired with Python (librosa / MIDIUtil) for prototyping acoustic scales.
  • Frontend Interface: React, HTML5/CSS3, and Canvas API to synchronize the EIC visual playback seamlessly with real-time audio waveforms and accessible keyboard controls.

Creativity & Design Philosophy

Most data sonification tools produce harsh, clinical sine waves that cause listener fatigue. Drawing from my experience co-hosting a youth space podcast and volunteering at a science museum, I designed Pulse of Terra around musicality and storytelling:

  • Consonant Harmonic Scales: Instead of random pitches, data anomalies modulate within carefully chosen pentatonic and modal scales, turning alarming climate trends into emotionally compelling, recognizable motifs (e.g., shifting from serene major harmonies to tense minor chords as anomalies spike).
  • Tactile Jukebox Metaphor: The UI mimics a classic jukebox, framing scientific datasets as "records" you can queue, scrub through, and remix—lowering the intimidation barrier for students and the general public.

Key Factors Considered

  • Accessibility First (WCAG Compliance): Full screen-reader compatibility, high-contrast visualizers, and keyboard-first navigation ensure blind and low-vision users can independently explore NASA datasets.
  • Scientific Fidelity vs. Aesthetics: Every musical shift is strictly proportional to underlying quantitative changes in the EIC frames, ensuring the audio remains an accurate scientific instrument rather than arbitrary background music.
  • Zero-Install Performance: Built as a lightweight web app so museum kiosks, classrooms, and personal devices can run real-time sonification smoothly without specialized hardware.

Benefits & Intended Impact

Pulse of Terra democratizes access to NASA’s Earth science. For blind and low-vision communities, it removes a major barrier to STEM engagement by offering an independent, non-visual way to analyze planetary data. For educators, science museums, and the broader public, turning abstract climate charts into visceral auditory experiences fosters deeper empathy, intuitive pattern recognition, and lasting awareness of how rapidly our home planet is changing.
